references.text: Jair had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkey colts, and they had thirty towns—a similar pattern of thirty descendants among a judge in Israel.
Abdon had forty sons and thirty grandsons—a similar pattern of many descendants among the judges of Israel.
Gideon had seventy sons and many wives—a similar theme about judges with many children and marital alliances.
Abraham sent out to find a wife for his son from another place—similar practice of bringing brides from outside for their sons.
The introduction to Ibzan's period as judge—the direct context for this verse.
The conclusion of Ibzan's life and burial—the immediate continuation of the narrative.
